main_body: Beehive thatched hut: a large conical straw roof over a low clay wall with an arched door
top_band: The thatched roof (rows ~2-56, light gold #d8bb68/#bc9a45 with darker courses) reads as a large sloped top surface. It is separated by a dark eave line (rows 55-57) from the wall face below.
evidence: The roof is a big overhanging thatch cone whose slopes face the viewer and the light. Below it the clay wall (rows ~57-77) sits in dark eave shadow, with a stone-grey base strip. The door is inset: a wood frame, dark interior and an arched hood cut into the thatch. This follows the same roof-over-wall structure as the Beodeul house references, so the roof slopes are visible from above and the front face is clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 lightness steps, with course lines and per-straw tick marks. The wall has grain bricks and a stone base with speckle. The outline is a tinted dark brown (7% neutral, matching the references). The measured facts are lower than the references: 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. Flat-fill coverage is 12%, mostly the dark door interior and parts of the wall. That is a modest gap, and the piece is a simple single-material hut, so it is acceptable next to the references.
